title: How to Use Annuities for Guaranteed Retirement Income
description: SPIA vs. Variable Annuities: When to buy a pension.
content:
Annuities are the most controversial product in finance. Some advisors hate them (high fees); others love them (guaranteed income). The truth is, 'Annuity' is a broad term covering both terrible products and excellent tools. For a retiree terrified of running out of money, a **Single Premium Immediate Annuity (SPIA)** is a powerful safety net. You trade a lump sum of cash for a guaranteed monthly paycheck for life, essentially buying yourself a pension. This guide separates the good annuities from the bad.

Key Takeaways

  • The 'Longevity Insurance': The primary value of an annuity is that it pays you even if you live to 105. It transfers the risk of 'living too long' from you to the insurance company.
  • SPIA (The Good): Simple, transparent, low fees. You give $200k, they give you $1,200/month forever. It functions like a bond that never matures.
  • Variable/Indexed (The Bad): Often loaded with 2-3% annual fees, surrender charges, and complex caps on returns. Avoid these unless you have a very specific tax need.
  • The 'Floor' Strategy: Use an annuity only to cover your *essential* expenses (Food/Housing) that Social Security doesn't cover. Keep the rest of your money in stocks for growth.

Why It Matters (US Context)

With fewer private pensions, the SPIA is the only way to manufacture guaranteed income. Interest rates impact payouts. Buying an annuity when rates are high (like 2024-2025) locks in a higher monthly check for life.

Annuity vs. 4% Rule

Scenario: 65-year-old male with $200,000.

Option A: The Investment Portfolio

Strategy: Keep $200k in 60/40 Stocks/Bonds. Withdraw 4%.
Income: $8,000/year ($666/mo).
Risk: Market crash could deplete principal.
Legacy: Whatever is left goes to heirs.

Option B: The SPIA

Strategy: Give $200k to insurance company.
Income: ~$14,000/year ($1,166/mo) based on current rates.
Risk: Inflation (unless you buy a COLA rider).
Legacy: $0. When you die, the money is gone (unless you buy 'Period Certain').

The Verdict: The annuity produces significantly higher cash flow (7% payout rate vs 4%) because you are spending down the principal ('Mortality Credits').

Buying Guide

  1. Shop Around: Rates vary by 10-20% between carriers. Use a comparison tool like Blueprint Income or ImmediateAnnuities.com. Do not just buy what your local broker sells.
  2. Check Credit Ratings: You are relying on the insurance company to exist in 30 years. Only buy from A++ rated carriers (NY Life, MassMutual, etc.).
  3. Don't Go 'All In': Never put more than 30-40% of your net worth in annuities. You lose liquidity. You need cash for emergencies.
  4. Consider a QLAC: A 'Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract' allows you to use IRA money (up to $200k) to buy an annuity that starts paying at age 85. It reduces RMDs now and provides 'Old Age' insurance.

Frequently Asked Questions

What if I die tomorrow?

In a standard Life-Only SPIA, the money is gone. To prevent this, buy 'Life with 20 Year Period Certain'. If you die in year 2, your heirs get the checks for the next 18 years. It lowers the monthly payout slightly but protects the principal.

Are annuities taxed?

If bought with IRA money (Qualified), the income is 100% taxable. If bought with Cash (Non-Qualified), only the earnings portion is taxable (Exclusion Ratio).

Does it protect against inflation?

Standard SPIAs do not. You can buy an 'Inflation Rider', but it lowers the starting payout by ~20-30%. It is usually better to keep a separate stock portfolio to fight inflation.
